ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Answer their wish on the Wishes page: grant it, promise it, or turn it down. It goes as soon as the wish isn't waiting any more, and a promise is enough.
A meeting has to choose one idea. It fades within three days. Choosing the idea most of the meeting backed avoids the bigger sting, and their idea can come back at the next meeting.
Repeal the decree on the Decrees page, or let it run out. It's felt from a disliked decree's second day, and more by those who hate it or whose request to repeal it has waited a day.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Repeal it, or wait it out

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: The council let a friend's promised wish lapse. It fades in a few days. Promise only what the colony can do in time, and check promised wishes on the Wishes page before they run out.

Envy of a rival who was honored, or who now outdoes them at their own craft. It fades in a few days, and stops coming once the two aren't rivals; time apart helps mend a rivalry. Kind colonists don't feel it, and the jealousy setting turns it off.

Not everyone will agree with every answer. It fades in two or three days. A colony whose answers keep going one way will keep upsetting those whose nature goes the other; the Our ways page shows who minds what.
Small, and gone in a day. Before a feast, have enough cooked meals in store for everyone; hold gatherings under a roof in wet weather, and bring people home for them if you can.

Something they built is gone. It fades in a few days. Walls and firefighting keep work standing, and think twice before tearing down anything built in the last 60 days; taking a building down to put a better one in its place doesn't count.
Cut blighted plants at once so the blight doesn't spread, and harvest before the first frost, or sow crops that ripen in time. A greenhouse keeps a field safe from frost.
Give the work to whoever is best at it, and build a proper workbench where the colony can; a crafting spot is slow and makeshift. Only those who care about the craft mind.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Let the best hand do it

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: An operation they did went wrong. It fades in a few days; a better doctor, good medicine, a clean hospital bed and a sterile room make operations go wrong less often.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Use a better doctor next time

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Put a stockpile near where things are made, mined or harvested, so loads don't cross the whole map.
Pick a research project. It goes as soon as one is under way.
Give doctoring a high priority in the Work tab, to more than one colonist, and keep medicine where the doctors can reach it.
A dining room under a roof, with tables and chairs near where people work. It's only felt outdoors in freezing cold or rain.

Something of theirs was sold. It fades in a few days. Art by people no longer here, or by the greedy, can be sold without hurt feelings; an animal with a master is missed by them, so sell the ones that answer to nobody.

Improve their bedroom: more space, a good floor, art, better furniture. It goes once their room is within two grades of the best one. Ascetics don't mind, and the game's own jealous colonists have their own mood for it.
Fix the cause: a freezer for the food and the rotten stock cleared out, a duster or parka for whoever works in the rain, and junk hauled out of the bedrooms.
A friendship gone cold. It fades in a few days. Friendships drift when opinions fall; time together (meals, recreation, the same work) can bring them back.
Keep loud work (building, mining, smithing) out of the night in the schedule, or away from bedrooms.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Keep loud work away from beds

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A small friction between two people who live too close: a borrowed thing, a seat, a joke, a snore. It fades within a day or two. Bedrooms of their own, enough room at the table and in the rec room, and keeping those who dislike each other apart mean fewer of them.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Fades within a day or two

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A friction that followed something real: a meal that made people sick, a mental break, shared work, a lent tool. It fades within a day or two. A clean kitchen and a skilled cook prevent the food poisoning behind the first.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Fades within a day or two

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: Someone they care about is ill. Care for them: a hospital bed, a good doctor, medicine. It goes when they recover.
Someone they care about is with a caravan in trouble. Bring the caravan home, buy or forage food on the way, or rest until whoever is down can walk.
It ends when the nemesis is captured or killed, and fades 60 days after what they did. Steadfast and iron-willed colonists, and psychopaths, don't feel it.
A people helped the colony and haven't been paid back, and kind colonists mind. Do them a good turn: a gift, a prisoner set free, help when they ask. The World page shows what they remember.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Do that people a good turn

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A hard week has them thinking of home. It fades in two days; something good helps it pass: a fine meal, a party, time with friends.

Fewer kinds of recreation at home than they expect, and no party or gathering in ten days. Build a new kind of recreation (horseshoes, a chess table, an instrument), or bring people together: any party, feast or gathering ends it.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.act: Build a new kind of recreation
